Topics.Title: Introduction to AI Providers in PreseMaker
Topics.Summary: An overview of the four AI providers supported by PreseMaker and how they are used to handle text-based generation tasks. This topic establishes the foundational context for configuring and working with AI providers.

Elements.Title: What PreseMaker Uses AI Providers For
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker relies on AI providers exclusively for text-based generation tasks across the course-building workflow.
Elements.Notes: Examples of text tasks include generating module topics, learning outcomes, slide content, text lessons, quiz questions, assignments, interactive-activity content, speaker narration, and standards.

Items.Text: Every AI task PreseMaker performs is text-based — there are no image generation or vision tasks of any kind.
AI providers are invoked across a wide range of content types, from quizzes and assignments to narration and standards.
Understanding that all tasks are text-based helps set accurate expectations about what configuring an AI provider will affect.

Elements.Title: The Four Supported AI Providers
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker supports exactly four AI providers: Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), GPT-4o (OpenAI), and Mistral AI.
Elements.Notes: Each provider requires its own API key obtained directly from the respective provider's platform before it can be used in PreseMaker.

Items.Text: The four providers are Claude by Anthropic, Gemini by Google, GPT-4o by OpenAI, and Mistral AI.
You do not need API keys for all four providers — having a key for at least one is sufficient to use PreseMaker's AI features.
Each provider's key is entered separately in PreseMaker's Settings area.

Elements.Title: How API Keys Are Stored and Secured
Elements.BodyText: When you enter an API key into PreseMaker's Settings, the application encrypts and stores it securely on your local machine.
Elements.Notes: This storage mechanism ensures that keys remain private to the individual user and are never exposed through course files or shared repositories.

Items.Text: PreseMaker encrypts each API key using Windows DPAPI and saves it in the app_settings.json file under your local user profile.
API keys are never embedded in a course file or shared with any repository, keeping them tied to the individual user's machine.
This means each user who needs to run AI features must configure their own API key in their own installation of PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: The Active AI Provider Setting
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker uses a single Active AI Provider setting in Settings to determine which provider handles all AI requests.
Elements.Notes: This is the central configuration point for AI behavior in PreseMaker — selecting a provider here affects every AI-powered feature in the application without exception.

Items.Text: In Settings, an Active AI Provider dropdown lets you designate which of the four supported providers will be used.
Whichever provider is selected becomes responsible for every AI task PreseMaker performs, across all content types.
Changing the active provider in Settings immediately redirects all subsequent AI requests to the newly selected provider.

Elements.Title: One Provider Handles Every Task — No Per-Task Routing
Elements.BodyText: There is no mechanism in PreseMaker to assign different AI providers to different types of tasks — one active provider serves all tasks universally.
Elements.Notes: An earlier version of PreseMaker did include per-task provider assignment, but it was removed because it caused user confusion, particularly when a key was entered for one provider while another provider was still routed to unkeyed tasks, resulting in failures.

Items.Text: There is no routing table, per-task dropdown, or any way to send slide generation to one provider and quiz generation to another.
The concept of a 'default provider for unassigned tasks' does not exist in the current version of PreseMaker.
This single-provider model was introduced deliberately to eliminate a class of configuration errors that arose from the previous per-task assignment approach.
When configuring PreseMaker, users should expect that every AI feature — narration, outcomes, quizzes, activities, and all others — will use the one selected active provider.

Topics.Title: Obtaining and Entering API Keys
Topics.Summary: How to acquire an API key from a supported AI provider and enter it in PreseMaker's Settings. This topic also covers how keys are securely stored using Windows DPAPI and what minimum key requirements exist.

Elements.Title: The Four Supported AI Providers
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker is compatible with four AI providers, each requiring its own API key obtained directly from the provider's platform.
Elements.Notes: The four providers are Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), GPT-4o (OpenAI), and Mistral AI. You do not need keys for all four providers — having one valid key is sufficient to use PreseMaker's AI features.

Items.Text: Each provider is a separate company with its own developer portal where API keys are created and managed.
Visit the provider's official website or developer console to sign up and generate your API key.
You only need to obtain a key from one provider to get started with PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Acquiring an API Key from a Provider
Elements.BodyText: To obtain an API key, you must create a developer or API account with your chosen AI provider and generate a key through their platform.
Elements.Notes: Each provider's process differs slightly, but all four — Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and Mistral AI — offer a developer console or API section in their account settings where keys can be generated.

Items.Text: Navigate to the official developer portal of your chosen provider (e.g., console.anthropic.com for Claude, platform.openai.com for GPT-4o).
Create or log in to your account and locate the API Keys section to generate a new key.
Copy the key immediately after generation, as many providers will not display it again after you leave the page.

Elements.Title: Entering Your API Key in PreseMaker Settings
Elements.BodyText: Once you have your API key, you enter it in PreseMaker's Settings panel, where it is associated with the corresponding provider.
Elements.Notes: Each of the four supported providers has its own dedicated key field in Settings. You only need to fill in the field for the provider you intend to use.

Items.Text: Open the Settings panel in PreseMaker and locate the API key entry fields for the supported providers.
Paste your copied API key into the field that corresponds to the provider you obtained it from.
Save your settings to confirm the key is stored and ready for use.

Elements.Title: Secure Storage with Windows DPAPI
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker encrypts every API key using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) before storing it, ensuring keys are protected at rest on your machine.
Elements.Notes: DPAPI encryption ties the key to your Windows user profile, meaning only your user account on that machine can decrypt and use the stored keys.

Items.Text: After you enter and save an API key, PreseMaker immediately encrypts it using Windows DPAPI.
The encrypted key is stored in the app_settings.json file located under your Windows user profile directory.
Keys stored this way are bound to your user account and cannot be decrypted by other users on the same machine.

Elements.Title: Keys Are Never Shared or Stored in Course Files
Elements.BodyText: API keys remain entirely local to your machine and are never embedded in course content or transmitted to a repository.
Elements.Notes: This is an important privacy and security boundary — sharing a course file or publishing to a repository will never expose your API credentials to other users.

Items.Text: API keys are stored only in your local app_settings.json file, not inside any course project file.
When you share, export, or push a course to a repository, no API key data is included.
Other collaborators or learners who receive your course content will never have access to your credentials.

Elements.Title: Minimum Key Requirements
Elements.BodyText: You do not need to configure API keys for all four providers — a single valid key for one provider is the minimum requirement to enable AI features in PreseMaker.
Elements.Notes: Having only one key is by design; the active provider you select in Settings will handle all AI tasks, so additional keys are only needed if you want the option to switch providers.

Items.Text: At least one valid API key must be entered in Settings before any AI-powered feature in PreseMaker can function.
You may optionally enter keys for multiple providers if you want the flexibility to switch between them in the Active AI Provider dropdown.
If a key is invalid or missing for the selected active provider, AI requests will fail — ensure the key you enter matches the active provider you have chosen.

Topics.Title: The Active AI Provider Setting
Topics.Summary: An explanation of the single Active AI Provider dropdown in Settings and how the selected provider handles every AI task in PreseMaker. This topic clarifies that one provider is responsible for all generation work simultaneously.

Elements.Title: What the Active AI Provider Setting Is
Elements.BodyText: In PreseMaker's Settings, there is a single dropdown called the Active AI Provider, which determines which AI service handles all generation work in the application.
Elements.Notes: This dropdown is the central control point for all AI functionality in PreseMaker. There is no other location in the application where an AI provider is selected.

Items.Text: The Active AI Provider dropdown is found in the Settings area of PreseMaker.
Whichever provider is selected in this dropdown becomes solely responsible for every AI task the application performs.
Only one provider can be active at any given time.

Elements.Title: One Provider Covers Every AI Task
Elements.BodyText: The selected Active AI Provider handles all text-based generation tasks in PreseMaker simultaneously — there is no division of responsibility between providers.
Elements.Notes: This is the single most important fact to understand about PreseMaker's AI configuration. Tasks covered include: module topics, learning outcomes, slide content, text lessons, quizzes, assignments, interactive activities, narration, and standards.

Items.Text: Every AI task PreseMaker performs — from generating module topics to quiz questions to speaker narration — is routed to the single active provider.
There is no scenario in which one task goes to one provider while a different task goes to another.
Selecting a provider in the dropdown immediately makes it responsible for all current and future AI generation until the setting is changed.

Elements.Title: No Per-Task Provider Assignment Exists
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker does not allow you to assign different AI providers to different types of tasks; the application has no routing table or per-task dropdown of any kind.
Elements.Notes: An earlier version of PreseMaker did include per-task provider assignment, but it was removed because it caused user confusion — for example, a user could enter only one provider's key and still encounter failures when tasks were silently routed to a different, unconfigured provider.

Items.Text: There is no mechanism to send slide generation to one provider and quiz generation to another.
There is no 'default provider for unassigned tasks' concept — a single selection governs everything.
Do not attempt to configure task-level routing; no such option exists in the current version of PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Why a Single Active Provider Simplifies Configuration
Elements.BodyText: The single Active AI Provider model was designed to eliminate the confusion that arose when different tasks were silently routed to different providers, which could cause unexpected failures.
Elements.Notes: When only one provider is active, the cause of any failure is unambiguous — the issue is isolated to the single configured provider rather than requiring the user to diagnose which task-level route failed.

Items.Text: A unified provider setting means that if generation succeeds for one task, the same provider and key will be used for all other tasks.
Users no longer need to worry about gaps in configuration where some tasks have no assigned provider.
Troubleshooting is straightforward: only one provider's key and status need to be checked when an error occurs.

Elements.Title: Choosing Which Provider to Make Active
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker supports four AI providers — Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), GPT-4o (OpenAI), and Mistral AI — and you select the one you want to use from the Active AI Provider dropdown after entering its API key.
Elements.Notes: You do not need API keys for all four providers. Having a valid key for at least one provider and setting it as active is sufficient to use all AI features in PreseMaker.

Items.Text: You must first obtain an API key from your chosen provider and enter it in Settings before that provider can be selected as active.
Only one key is required — you do not need accounts with all four providers.
Switching the active provider is as simple as selecting a different entry in the dropdown, provided that provider's key has also been entered.

Topics.Title: Understanding That There Is No Per-Task Provider Assignment
Topics.Summary: A focused clarification that PreseMaker does not support routing different task types to different providers, and why that feature was removed. This topic corrects common misconceptions and explains the simplified single-provider model.

Elements.Title: The Single-Provider Rule
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker uses exactly one active AI provider for every task it performs, with no exceptions.
Elements.Notes: This is the single most important architectural fact about PreseMaker's AI configuration. All task types — from slide content to quizzes — flow through the same provider.

Items.Text: The Active AI Provider dropdown in Settings is the one and only place where a provider is selected.
Whichever provider is selected there handles all AI tasks: module topics, learning outcomes, slide content, text lessons, quizzes, assignments, interactive activities, narration, and standards.
There is no secondary or fallback provider that handles tasks when the primary is busy or unavailable.

Elements.Title: What Per-Task Assignment Means — and Why It Does Not Exist
Elements.BodyText: Per-task provider assignment would mean routing specific task types — such as quizzes or narration — to different AI providers, but PreseMaker does not support this.
Elements.Notes: Understanding what the feature would look like helps users recognize that nothing in the interface corresponds to it and stops them from searching for controls that do not exist.

Items.Text: There is no routing table, no per-task dropdown, and no way to send one kind of content generation to one provider and another kind to a different provider.
You cannot configure slide generation to use GPT-4o while quiz generation uses Claude — all tasks go to the single active provider.
No concept of a 'default provider for unassigned tasks' exists in PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Why the Feature Was Removed
Elements.BodyText: An earlier version of PreseMaker did include per-task provider assignment, but it was deliberately removed because it caused significant user confusion.
Elements.Notes: Knowing the history helps users understand that the simplification was intentional and based on real user-experience problems, not an oversight.

Items.Text: The core problem was that a user could enter an API key for one provider yet still encounter failures when a specific task was routed to a different provider for which no key had been entered.
This mismatch between the key a user thought was active and the key actually required for a given task made errors difficult to diagnose and resolve.
Removing per-task assignment eliminated that entire class of configuration error by ensuring one key and one provider covers everything.

Elements.Title: Correcting Common Misconceptions
Elements.BodyText: Because per-task routing existed in an older version, some users arrive with the expectation that different tasks can still be sent to different providers.
Elements.Notes: Directly addressing misconceptions reduces the chance that users will waste time looking for controls that no longer exist or misinterpret error messages.

Items.Text: If you previously used an older version of PreseMaker with per-task assignment, that workflow no longer applies — the current version has no such controls.
There is no hidden or advanced setting that re-enables per-task routing; the feature is fully removed from the application.
API failures are not caused by tasks being routed to an unconfigured provider; with the single-provider model, every failure points to the one active provider.

Elements.Title: Practical Implication: One Key Is All You Need
Elements.BodyText: Because every task uses the same provider, you only need to obtain and configure a single API key to use all of PreseMaker's AI features.
Elements.Notes: This simplifies onboarding significantly — users do not need accounts with multiple AI providers unless they want the option to switch.

Items.Text: Entering a valid API key for one provider in Settings is sufficient to enable every AI-powered feature in PreseMaker.
You may enter keys for multiple providers if you want the flexibility to switch the active provider, but only the currently selected one is ever used.
Switching providers is done by changing the Active AI Provider dropdown — from that point forward, all tasks use the newly selected provider.

Topics.Title: Using the Prompt Button to Inspect AI Requests
Topics.Summary: How to use the Prompt button to view the exact text sent to the active AI provider before or during generation. This topic helps learners understand and verify the input their chosen provider receives.

Elements.Title: What the Prompt Button Does
Elements.BodyText: The Prompt button allows you to inspect the exact text that PreseMaker will send to your active AI provider before or during generation.
Elements.Notes: This is a transparency feature — it gives you a direct window into the input your provider receives, helping you understand what is driving the AI's output.

Items.Text: Clicking the Prompt button displays the full text of the request PreseMaker has constructed for the current task.
The text shown is precisely what the active AI provider will receive — no hidden additions or modifications occur after display.
This works for any text-based task, including module topics, learning outcomes, slide content, quizzes, assignments, narration, and standards.

Elements.Title: When to Use the Prompt Button
Elements.BodyText: The Prompt button is most useful when you want to verify, troubleshoot, or simply understand the input being sent before committing to a full generation.
Elements.Notes: Inspecting the prompt before generation can save time by catching issues — such as missing context or unexpected phrasing — before they result in poor AI output.

Items.Text: Use it before generation to confirm the request looks correct for the task you are performing.
Use it during troubleshooting to determine whether unexpected AI output stems from the prompt itself or from the provider's response.
Because the same active provider handles every task, reviewing the prompt helps confirm the right provider is receiving the right request.

Elements.Title: Understanding the Text Shown in the Prompt
Elements.BodyText: All AI tasks in PreseMaker are text-based, so every prompt you inspect will be a text request — there are no image or vision requests.
Elements.Notes: PreseMaker does not generate images and has no vision tasks. Every prompt you will ever inspect through the Prompt button is a text-only request.

Items.Text: The displayed prompt reflects the specific task context, such as the course structure, topic details, or content settings relevant to that generation step.
No image generation or vision-related content will appear in any prompt, as PreseMaker exclusively performs text-based AI tasks.
The prompt is constructed by PreseMaker automatically; the Prompt button reveals this constructed text without requiring you to edit it.

Elements.Title: The Prompt Reflects Your Active Provider Selection
Elements.BodyText: Because PreseMaker uses a single active AI provider for all tasks, the prompt you inspect is always destined for that one selected provider.
Elements.Notes: There is no per-task routing, so you do not need to wonder which provider will receive a given prompt — it is always the active provider set in Settings.

Items.Text: The Active AI Provider dropdown in Settings determines who receives every prompt, including the one displayed when you click the Prompt button.
If you switch your active provider in Settings, subsequent prompts will be sent to the newly selected provider.
Verifying the prompt is especially helpful after changing providers, to ensure the request format and content are still producing the results you expect.

Elements.Title: Verifying Input to Diagnose Generation Issues
Elements.BodyText: The Prompt button is a practical diagnostic tool when AI output does not match your expectations, letting you rule out input-side problems.
Elements.Notes: If the prompt looks correct but the output is still wrong or fails, the issue likely lies with the provider's response or API configuration rather than the prompt itself.

Items.Text: Inspecting the prompt lets you confirm that the correct course context and task details were included in the request.
If the prompt text appears incomplete or incorrect, adjusting your course content or settings before regenerating can improve results.
If the prompt looks accurate but failures still occur, the next step is to investigate your API key configuration or provider availability rather than the prompt content.

Topics.Title: Interpreting and Responding to Generation Failures
Topics.Summary: What generation failure messages mean and how to respond to them effectively. This topic guides learners through diagnosing common causes of failed AI requests and taking corrective action.

Elements.Title: What a Generation Failure Means
Elements.BodyText: A generation failure occurs when PreseMaker sends a request to the active AI provider and does not receive a successful response.
Elements.Notes: Because one active provider handles every AI task, a failure on any task — whether generating slide content, quiz questions, or narration — points back to the same provider and the same potential root causes.

Items.Text: Generation failures are not content errors; they are communication or configuration errors between PreseMaker and the active AI provider.
Any AI task can trigger a failure: module topics, learning outcomes, slide content, text lessons, quizzes, assignments, interactive activities, narration, and standards.
The failure message is your first diagnostic clue — read it carefully before taking corrective action.

Elements.Title: Common Cause: Missing or Invalid API Key
Elements.BodyText: The most frequent cause of a generation failure is that the API key for the active provider is absent, incorrectly entered, or has been revoked by the provider.
Elements.Notes: API keys are obtained directly from the provider's developer portal. An easy mistake is entering a key that belongs to a different provider than the one currently selected as active.

Items.Text: Open Settings and confirm that an API key is entered for the provider shown in the Active AI Provider dropdown.
If a key is present, verify it matches the selected provider — for example, an Anthropic key must be paired with Claude, not GPT-4o.
If the key was recently regenerated on the provider's side, you must update it in PreseMaker Settings to restore connectivity.

Elements.Title: Common Cause: Wrong Active Provider Selected
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker uses a single Active AI Provider for every task, so selecting a provider whose key has not been entered will cause all AI requests to fail.
Elements.Notes: This was a documented source of confusion in an earlier version that supported per-task assignment — users would enter one provider's key but have a different provider set as active, resulting in failures across all tasks.

Items.Text: Navigate to Settings and check the Active AI Provider dropdown to confirm it matches the provider whose key you have entered.
You only need one valid API key; whichever provider that key belongs to should be set as the active provider.
Switching the active provider to match your entered key is often the fastest fix for unexplained generation failures.

Elements.Title: Common Cause: Provider-Side Issues
Elements.BodyText: Even with a correct key and active provider, failures can occur due to outages, rate limits, or quota exhaustion on the provider's platform.
Elements.Notes: Rate limits and quota exhaustion are especially common during heavy use sessions. Checking the provider's status page or usage dashboard can confirm whether the issue is on their end.

Items.Text: If your key and active provider settings appear correct, check the provider's service status page for ongoing outages.
Exceeding your account's usage quota or hitting a rate limit will cause requests to fail until the limit resets or your plan is upgraded.
Waiting a short time and retrying is appropriate when rate limiting is suspected.

Elements.Title: Diagnosing the Failure: A Step-by-Step Approach
Elements.BodyText: Effective diagnosis follows a consistent order: verify the active provider, verify the key, then look outward to the provider's platform.

Items.Text: Step 1 — Open Settings and confirm which provider is selected in the Active AI Provider dropdown.
Step 2 — Confirm that a valid, current API key for that exact provider is entered and saved.
Step 3 — If both are correct, check the provider's status page or your account dashboard for quota or outage issues.
Step 4 — Retry the failed task after making any correction; because all tasks use the same provider, a fix will restore all AI features simultaneously.

Elements.Title: Taking Corrective Action
Elements.BodyText: Once the cause is identified, corrective actions are straightforward and typically require only a Settings update or a provider account action.
Elements.Notes: Because keys are encrypted with Windows DPAPI and stored locally, re-entering a key is safe and does not affect any course files or shared repositories.

Items.Text: To fix a missing key, obtain the API key from the provider's developer portal and enter it in PreseMaker Settings.
To fix a mismatched active provider, change the Active AI Provider dropdown to match the key you have on hand, or enter the correct key for the currently selected provider.
To fix a quota or rate-limit issue, wait for the limit to reset, upgrade your provider plan, or temporarily switch the active provider to one with an available key.
